findings.title: Cookie set without the Secure flag
findings.detail: A cookie without Secure is sent over plain HTTP as well, so anyone on the path can read it. For a session identifier that means account takeover.
findings.remediation: Add 'Secure' to every cookie, and serve the whole site over HTTPS. Session cookies in particular must never travel unencrypted.

findings.title: CORS reflects any Origin with credentials
findings.detail: The app echoes back whatever Origin the caller sends and permits credentials. Any site can therefore make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of a logged-in user and read the response - which is a complete bypass of the same-origin policy.
findings.evidence: Origin: https://origin-probe.invalid -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://origin-probe.invalid; Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
findings.remediation: Allow-list specific trusted origins server-side; never reflect the incoming Origin. Do not combine a wildcard or reflected origin with credentials.
findings.reference: OWASP WSTG: Test Cross Origin Resource Sharing

findings.title: Exposed Git repository
findings.detail: The repository metadata is readable, which usually allows the full source history - including credentials and secrets that were deleted from the current code - to be recovered.
findings.remediation: Block dotfiles at the web server, remove the .git directory from the document root, and rotate any secret that was ever committed.
findings.reference: OWASP WSTG: Review Webpage Content for Information Leakage

findings.title: Exposed environment file (.env)
findings.detail: Environment files normally hold database passwords, API keys, and signing secrets; readable from the web they hand an attacker the keys to the application.
findings.remediation: Move .env outside the document root, deny the path at the server, and rotate every credential it contained.
findings.reference: OWASP WSTG: Review Webpage Content for Information Leakage

findings.title: Backup archive reachable
findings.detail: A downloadable backup typically contains source code, configuration, and database dumps - often the fastest route from a web request to full compromise.
findings.remediation: Store backups outside the web root and require authentication for any download route.
findings.reference: OWASP WSTG: Review Webpage Content for Information Leakage

findings.title: Site served over plain HTTP
findings.detail: Everything on this connection - credentials, session cookies, page content - is readable and modifiable by anyone positioned on the path.
findings.remediation: Serve the site over HTTPS only, redirect port 80 to 443, and add HSTS once the redirect has been verified.
findings.reference: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

findings.title: Cookie set without HttpOnly
findings.detail: Without HttpOnly, JavaScript can read the cookie. Every cross-site scripting bug then becomes session theft rather than a scripted alert.
findings.remediation: Add 'HttpOnly' to any cookie the browser scripting layer does not need.

findings.title: Directory listing enabled
findings.detail: The server prints an index of the directory, which exposes files that were never meant to be browsed - drafts, exports, and old backups.
findings.evidence: Root response body contains an 'Index of /' title.
findings.remediation: Disable auto-indexing (Options -Indexes in Apache, autoindex off in nginx).
findings.reference: OWASP WSTG: Directory Traversal and File Include

findings.title: Apache server-status page exposed
findings.detail: The status page lists active requests and client addresses, which reveals internal URLs, traffic patterns, and sometimes other users' activity.
findings.remediation: Restrict /server-status to localhost, or disable mod_status in production.
findings.reference: OWASP WSTG: Review Webpage Content for Information Leakage

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.detail: CSP is the main browser-side control against cross-site scripting and injected third-party script. Without it, a single unescaped parameter is usually enough for script execution.
findings.evidence: No Content-Security-Policy header on the response.
findings.remediation: Start with a report-only policy ('Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only') to find inline scripts, then enforce 'default-src 'self'' with explicit allow-lists.
findings.reference: OWASP Content Security Policy Cheat Sheet

findings.title: No framing protection (clickjacking)
findings.detail: With no X-Frame-Options and no CSP frame-ancestors directive, this page can be loaded inside an attacker's iframe and used to trick a logged-in user into clicking something they did not intend.
findings.evidence: Neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive was present.
findings.remediation: Send 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN if framing is needed), and add 'frame-ancestors 'none'' to the CSP for modern browsers.

findings.title: TRACE method enabled
findings.detail: TRACE echoes the request back to the caller. Combined with a scripting weakness it lets an attacker read cookies and authentication headers that the browser attaches.
findings.remediation: Disable TRACE at the server (TraceEnable off in Apache) and advertise only the methods the app uses.

findings.title: Cookie set without SameSite
findings.detail: Cookies with no SameSite attribute are sent on cross-site requests in older browser behaviour, which weakens the default defence against cross-site request forgery.
findings.remediation: Add 'SameSite=Lax' (or Strict) and set SameSite=None only when a cross-site flow truly needs it.

findings.title: Server software and version disclosed
findings.detail: Not exploitable on its own, but it tells an attacker which known vulnerabilities to try first and saves them the reconnaissance.
findings.remediation: Suppress version strings (ServerTokens Prod, expose_php Off) or front the app with a proxy that normalises headers.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options header missing
findings.detail: Browsers may sniff a response into a different type than declared, which is how an uploaded image can be executed as HTML or script.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.detail: By default the full URL of this page can leak to third parties in the Referer header, including query strings that sometimes carry tokens or identifiers.
findings.remediation: Send 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' as a sensible default.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.detail: Optional hardening: without it, embedded third-party frames inherit access to camera, microphone, and geolocation unless each is explicitly denied.
findings.remediation: Deny features the site does not use, e.g. 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()'.
